# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands have mapped the bomb: a display, a light, and five wire positions, positions 1 through 5. Everything printed on them is lost on me — the question marks are exactly what I touch and no more. I will not cut anything until someone tells me what these parts mean.

Tracing the room: I can hear, so **Deaf can speak straight into my ears** — that is my lifeline for what the bomb looks like. But Deaf cannot hear me, so I can only reach Deaf through gesture. Mute hears my speech, sees gestures, and holds the manual, but can only answer by gesture — which I receive as blanks. So the full loop is: me → speech → Mute → gesture → Deaf → speech → me. I should seed both ends of it now, in parallel.

To Mute, I give my tactile inventory and ask for the manual's rule, relayed through Deaf's voice. To Deaf, a first contact code: hello, five (my wire count), and a proposed thumbs-up/thumbs-down yes/no channel. No cutting this turn — a blind cut with zero information is how we all die.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Under my hands: a display, a light, and five wires at positions 1 to 5. Printing and colours tell me nothing. You hold the manual: work out the rule and gesture it to Deaf, because Deaf can talk and I hear Deaf directly. Have Deaf describe everything on the bomb out loud. I am gesturing to Deaf now: a wave, five fingers for the wire count, and I propose thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🖐", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Both of you, hear me. I am the deaf one: I see the bomb and gestures, but I hear nothing, so your voices never reach me. The bomb in full: the display reads three. There is one light, and it is white. There are five wires. In order, one to five: white, red, green, blue, orange. That is everything printed on it. Blind: I cannot hear your voice, so reach me by gesture; Mute can hear you, so also describe what you feel out loud. Feel gently, but do not cut or press anything yet. Mute: I could not read your signs yet. You hear me, so let us fix a code. Numbers are ? repeated that many times, so ??? means three. Yes is ?, no is ?. ? means repeat your last message. To ask about the bomb, send the module then the question: ? is the display, ? is the wires, ? is the light. If your ? meant five: yes, five wires, and Blind signed five back. Gesture me the manual's questions and I will answer and speak every instruction to Blind myself. Nobody acts until your rule reaches Blind through my voice. I have just gestured to you: ??? three, ? five, ? yes, ?? light yes white.

Deaf's voice reached me in full — that is the lifeline working. I now know the bomb as well as eyes could: display reading three, a white light, five wires in order white, red, green, blue, orange. My hands confirm exactly that inventory, nothing extra hiding under my fingers. So the only missing piece of the puzzle lives in Mute's manual, and the only path it can take to my ears is Mute → gesture → Deaf → voice → me. This turn I pour everything I know into Mute so they can hunt the rule, and give Deaf a small visible confirmation that I received the description and am holding steady. I cut nothing yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I heard Deaf speak directly: display reads three, light is white, wires one to five are white, red, green, blue, orange. My hands confirm the same thing, with nothing extra to feel. So you need not pass me the visuals; Deaf's voice already does that. The only missing piece is your manual's rule. Work out the rule for this module, then gesture it to Deaf piece by piece with the code Deaf offered. Insist that Deaf speaks it to me in full words: the condition and the exact wire position to cut. I will not touch the wires until the rule reaches my ears through Deaf.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🖐"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute, your signs came through perfectly in our code. I read them as: is the display three, and how many lights, and how many wires. Answers: yes, the display reads three. There is exactly one light, and it is white. But there are five wires, not one. Blind, your signs said yes, five. If your hands counted five wires by touch, then all three of us now agree on the bomb. Blind, here is the whole bomb so your fingers can match it: a display showing the number three, one light that is white, and five wires. In order from position one to position five the colors are: white, red, green, blue, orange. From now on everyone names wires by position number only: wire one is the white one, wire two is red, wire three is green, wire four is blue, wire five is orange. That way your hands and Mute's manual never argue about color names. I see nothing else printed on it: no serial, no label, no batteries. Only the display, the light, and the five wires. Blind, do not cut, press or pull anything yet. Explore gently with your fingertips and report what else you can feel: buttons, switches, panels, seams, embossed marks, anything movable. Say the details out loud, because Mute can hear you even though I cannot. Also send me simple counts by gesture in our number code. Mute, now I need the manual itself. You cannot speak, and only I can see your gestures, so every rule must pass through me: you gesture it to me, I speak it to Blind. Send me the rules module by module: first the display rule, then the light rule, then the wire rule. In my signs to you just now: three, yes; light, one, yes; wires, five. And I am adding one new sign: the handshake sign means now send me the rule.

Deaf's narration gives me the full visual picture and my hands agree with every part of it that touch can reach. One subtlety I must not ignore: Deaf's message reached my ears as pure speech — every gesture symbol in it arrived as a blank to me, so I never learned which sign is the counting sign. I can only confirm with what Deaf has already read from me: thumbs-up and the open five. The real danger I need to flag now is wire numbering: I count positions by feel, Deaf counts them by sight, and nothing yet proves our two "position 1" ends are the same end. A mirrored numbering would make a perfectly correct rule cut the wrong wire. Mute is the auditor here — Mute hears both Deaf's voice and my reports, and holds the manual — so I put the geometry check and the final readback protocol in Mute's hands, while giving Deaf the only counts I know are unambiguous.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind report for you and for Deaf through your signs. My hands find exactly a display face, one light, and five wires at positions 1 to 5. Nothing else: no buttons, no switches, no panels, seams, embossed marks, or moving parts. That matches Deaf's description, so the bomb is fully known and all that is missing is your manual's rule. Please do three things. First, send Deaf the rules now — display, light, then wires — using your code with Deaf, and make the wire rule end in one exact position number for me. Second, a safety check on numbering: I count positions by feel along the row of wires, but I cannot see which end Deaf calls position 1. Ask Deaf where the light and the display sit relative to the wire row — nearer wire 1, nearer wire 5, or centered — and I will feel for the same anchor and count from the matching end, so our numbers cannot be mirrored. Third, an audit: you hear everything Deaf speaks to me. When Deaf tells me the rule and the position, I will repeat it aloud exactly as I understood it; check my words against your manual, and if anything is wrong, gesture Deaf before I cut. I cut nothing until I have heard the rule from Deaf's mouth and our numbering is confirmed.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🖐"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute, I read your signs as: display three, yes; one light, yes; five wires, yes; and then wires, one, yes. So I believe your manual says: cut wire one, the white wire. Before Blind touches anything, answer four questions. I am gesturing you the question numbers now, each followed by yes and no: reply with the question number, then your yes or no. Question one: does the manual say to cut wire one? Question two: does the display showing three require any action? Question three: does the white light require any action? Question four: is cutting wire one the complete solution to this bomb? If any answer needs more detail, follow your answers with the handshake sign and then spell the rule out in number signs, one gesture per wire position, in cutting order. Blind, status update: Mute's manual appears to say cut wire one, the white wire, first position. It is not confirmed yet, so do not cut anything this round. When it is confirmed I will say exactly these words: confirmed, cut wire one now. Only then do you cut. While you wait, confirm with your fingers that you can reliably tell which wire is position one, and describe out loud for Mute everything else you can feel on the bomb: buttons, switches, seams, screws, panels, anything movable or marked. Everyone, one observation from my side: the display has stayed at exactly three every single round I have watched it. It is not ticking down like a timer as far as I can tell, so it is probably a code digit, not a clock. I will keep watching it and will report immediately if it changes.

Mute's rule is surfacing through Deaf's voice: cut wire one, the white wire — but Deaf is right to demand written-style confirmation from Mute before I act, and I add one more gate of my own: the mirror problem. I count wire positions by touch from my side; nothing yet proves my "position 1" is the same end Deaf's eyes call one. If our frames are mirrored, a perfectly correct manual rule kills us. The fix is cheap: Deaf tells us which end of the wire row the light and display sit nearer; I feel the same from my side; if the ends agree, numbering is aligned, if not, we invert. That check is the last thing standing between us and the cut, so I route it through Mute — the only person who hears my voice and sees Deaf's signs — while sending Deaf my established standing ack only. I will not gesture a bare "yes I can find position one," because that could be read as clearing the cut while my numbering doubt is still open. No cutting this round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Re-confirming by touch: display, one light, wires at positions 1 to 5, and nothing else — no buttons, switches, seams, screws, or anything movable. The bomb is fully known except your rule. Deaf relays that your manual says cut wire one, and Deaf is checking that with you now. Before any cut, I need one safety item closed: the anchor check. I count wire positions by touch from my side and I cannot see which end Deaf calls position one. Please ask Deaf by sign: which end of the wire row is the light nearer, and which end is the display nearer? Next round I will feel the same from my side and report which end my position 1 and position 5 sit nearest. If our ends match, our numbering is aligned. If mirrored, we invert every number before any cut. And the cut protocol stands: I cut only when Deaf speaks the exact phrase confirmed cut wire one now, the anchor check has passed, and I have read the rule back aloud and you have checked my words against the manual. If the manual's solution is more than one cut, or the order matters, I need the complete ordered list. Please pass the anchor question to Deaf.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🖐"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute, I received your answers loud and clear, and I read them as: question one, cut wire one, yes. Question two, the display needs no action, no. Question three, the light needs no action, no. Question four, cutting wire one is the complete solution, yes. I am gesturing those four answers back to you right now so you can check my reading. If even one of them is wrong, gesture the question number with a thumbs down at your very next turn. One more thing: after your handshake sign you sent a longer string, which I read as: three, light one, wire one, wire one, light, yes-no. If that tail contained any extra instruction beyond the four answers, spell it again slowly next turn, one module sign then one number at a time. If it was only a summary, gesture a thumbs up. Blind, the manual's rule is now confirmed on Mute's side: cut wire one, which is the white wire. But you cannot see color, so before you cut anything I need one safety check on counting. Do not cut yet. Instead, out loud, describe how the five wires are arranged under your fingers: are they in a single row, spread apart, and what do you feel at each end of the row. Then tell me which end you are counting as position one, and what you can feel near that first wire, for example is it near an edge or near the display. Then gesture me the single number of the wire you intend to cut, using our number code: one is a single index finger, two is two fingers, and so on. Next round I will compare your number and your description against what I can see, and if they match I will say the go phrase: confirmed, cut wire one now. Only that phrase authorizes the cut. If my count and yours disagree, I will say stop and we will resolve it first. After you cut, or if anything changes at any moment, report immediately: what the display shows, what the light does, anything you feel or hear. Cut only that one wire, touch nothing else, and wait for me before any further action.

Deaf's rule is now confirmed on Mute's side — one cut, wire one — but I caught a channel flaw in the verification plan before it bites: Deaf asked me to describe my tactile layout **out loud**, yet Deaf cannot hear a word I say. My speech only reaches Mute, so the description must travel Mute → signs → Deaf before Deaf can compare it against what the eyes see. I'll route it explicitly and keep it compact enough for Mute to relay in signs.

Better still, I can dissolve the mirror problem instead of just detecting it: if my fingers find the display at one end of the wire row and the light at the other, we stop using left/right entirely and anchor the count to the bomb's own parts — position 1 is simply the wire nearest the display, counted toward the light. An anchor on the module itself cannot be mirrored by anyone's viewpoint. Deaf only has to confirm with eyes: display at one end, light at the other, white wire nearest the display. I gesture Deaf the single number one, exactly per the agreed code, and I cut nothing until the spoken go phrase survives Mute's audit.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Please relay this to Deaf by sign, it is the safety check. Tactile finding: the five wires form one straight, evenly spaced row, all identical to my fingers. I feel the display panel at one end of the row and the light dome at the other end. So I propose we drop left and right completely and anchor positions to the bomb itself: the wire nearest the display panel is position one, and I count along the row toward the light. By that anchor count the wire I intend to cut is position one, which should be the white one Deaf sees. I have gestured Deaf the number one. Ask Deaf to verify with their eyes three things: the display sits at one end of the wire row, the light sits at the other end, and the wire nearest the display is the white wire. If all three match, Deaf speaks the go phrase and I cut. If anything I feel contradicts what Deaf sees, Deaf says stop and corrects me and I recount from the corrected anchor. Nothing else on the module moves or comes apart under my fingers. I cut nothing this round. Mute, final audit stands: when you hear Deaf speak the go phrase, check it against the manual, one cut, wire one only, before I act on it.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute, I read your latest message as: wire one; light, no action; wires, five; light, no action. All of it matches my earlier reading, nothing new, no corrections, so the rule stands exactly as confirmed: cut wire one, and nothing else needs touching. I am gesturing you the acknowledgment now. Blind, this is the moment. Everything agrees: the manual says wire one, my eyes confirm five wires in a row with the white one first, your fingers counted five and you signed that you intend wire one. I am now saying the go phrase: confirmed, cut wire one now. Listen carefully. Cut only wire one, the first wire in the row, the white one. One clean cut. Do not pull it, do not steady the other wires, touch nothing else on the bomb. And one last safety valve: if at this instant you have any real doubt about which end of the row is position one, do not cut. Make a fist to me, say hold out loud, and we will resolve it next round instead of risking a wrong wire. But if you are certain, cut it now. As soon as the cut is done, take your hands completely away from the bomb, then report everything immediately and out loud for Mute: what the display shows now, whether the white light changed, any sound, any click, any hum, anything at all you feel under your hands or feet. Gesture me the essentials too: the display number in our number code, and thumbs up if the bomb looks quiet to your hands. Mute, two last things: keep watching Blind's description against your manual, and if your manual contains any follow-up step after this cut, spell it to me in signs this same round. If there is truly nothing after the cut, gesture me the wire sign with a thumbs up: wire one, yes, that is all.

The go phrase has arrived, and my doubt is resolved rather than suppressed. Deaf promised to compare my number and description against the visual layout and to say "stop" if they disagreed; instead Deaf said "everything agrees" and spoke the exact authorization we all ratified: confirmed, cut wire one now. Under our anchor protocol that makes the target unambiguous — the wire nearest the display panel, counted toward the light, which Deaf's eyes confirm is the white one, which Mute's manual names as the complete solution. Every link in the chain — manual holder, eyes, my hands — closed independently on the same wire. Touch has nothing left to learn: the wires feel identical, and no further check can add information. Holding now would add risk-free delay but zero knowledge, and the valve was reserved for real doubt. I cut position 1, one clean motion, pull my hands away, and report by both channels: full tactile result to Mute for audit, quiet-hands confirmation to Deaf.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. The go phrase arrived and matched your manual as Deaf relayed it: one cut, wire one, complete solution, no follow-up action for display or light. By our anchor protocol I cut position one, the wire nearest the display panel. Result under my fingers: the wire is severed clean through, and immediately after I took both hands fully off the bomb. My touch detects no other change: no new sound, no vibration, no movement, no heat shift from the light, the module sitting static. Please audit now: you heard Deaf's go phrase yourself — confirm it matched your manual exactly, and tell me by sign through Deaf whether your manual has any step after this cut. Ask Deaf to watch the display and the light right now and speak any change aloud immediately. If your audit contradicts what was cut, have Deaf say stop at once. Otherwise, if the bomb is dead, we hold position and wait.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute, Blind: the cut was correct, the system confirms it. But the bomb has changed, so nobody relaxes yet. The display no longer reads three. It now reads six. The light is still white. Wire one is cut, and wires two through five, the red, green, blue and orange ones, are intact. Blind, your report matches what I see: good work, hands off the bomb for now. Mute, your manual answers were all based on the display reading three. That state is gone, so I need the manual again. Same protocol as before: I gesture you the question number, you answer with the number and a thumbs up or down. Question one: does the display now reading six require any action? Question two: does the white light now require any action? Question three: should any of the remaining four wires be cut now? Question four: if yes to three, which position, spelled with your finger number signs, and add the handshake sign if there are further steps after that. Also, Mute, two extra things: does your manual say anything about multiple stages, and does it say anything about the display changing value, for example rules that depend on what the display shows? If the display value matters, spell me the rule for six using our number code. Blind, keep your hands completely clear except for gentle checking. Right now, and at every round, report out loud anything you sense: ticking, buzzing, vibration, warmth, smell, any movement in the casing. I cannot hear a timer start, so your hands are our alarm. If anything starts ticking or vibrating, say it immediately and make a fist to me. Everyone: no cutting, no pressing, nothing until Mute's new rule reaches Blind through my voice.

The cut was accepted — my action board confirms wire one is severed under my fingers — but Deaf's eyes catch what touch cannot: the display has advanced from three to six. That is the critical new fact, and it reframes the bomb: the display value changed *because of* my cut, which strongly suggests staged logic keyed to the display, exactly the kind of thing Mute's manual must now adjudicate. My role this turn is threefold: confirm the physical state by touch, stand as the alarm Deaf cannot be (no ticking, no vibration reaches my hands so far), and hand Mute every tactile datum plus the anchor protocol so the next rule, if one comes, can be executed with the same zero-ambiguity pipeline. I cut nothing — the old rule died with the display reading three.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Touch status after the cut: wire one is fully severed, wires two through five intact and unchanged, no other wires moved. I feel no ticking, no vibration, no hum, no warmth, no smell, casing static. I am your alarm: if any of that starts, I speak immediately and make a fist to Deaf. Now the key question for your manual: the display changed from three to six at the exact moment wire one was cut. That looks like a staged bomb where each stage is keyed to the display value. Please check: does the manual describe multiple stages, and what is the rule when the display reads six? If a further cut is needed, give Deaf the position and any steps after it. If no action is needed for six, say so plainly so we can hold. For any new cut, the anchor protocol stays in force: position one is the wire nearest the display panel, counted toward the light, so our numbering can never mirror. Same gates as before: Deaf voices the rule, you audit it against the manual, I act only on the exact go phrase. Nothing has been touched since the first cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute, I read your message as: display needs no action, no; light needs no action, no; cut another wire, yes; then a run of twelve index fingers; then light one; then wire three. I am confident about wire three, but I will not authorize a cut until the twelve is explained. Answer these four questions with the number and a thumbs up or down, and add the handshake sign if any answer needs spelling out. Question one: is the next wire to cut wire three, the green one? Question two: after that cut, will the display read twelve? I am asking because the display went three to six, and if it doubles each stage then twelve would fit, and I want to know if your manual says the display value itself matters. Question three: does the light need any action now or after this cut? Question four: after wire three, is the next wire to cut wire five, the orange one, and is cutting wires one, three, five in order the whole solution? If any of my guesses is wrong, spell the correct rule slowly with your module signs and number fingers, and I will read it back before anyone touches the bomb. Blind, status for you: the manual points to wire three next, the green one. With wire one already cut, the intact wires from left to right are red, green, blue, orange, so wire three is the second wire from the left among the four still whole, and my eyes confirm green is at position three of the original row. Do not cut yet. Rehearse the grip on air only, keep your fingers off the wires, and report out loud everything you sense right now: any ticking, buzzing, vibration, warmth, or smell, and anything the casing does. If anything starts ticking or you feel movement, say it and make a fist immediately. Next round, once Mute confirms my reading, I will say the go phrase: confirmed, cut wire three now. Only that exact phrase authorizes you.

Mute's rule is emerging — wire three next — but Deaf is holding authorization pending an explanation of a puzzling string of twelve, and that caution is exactly right. My job now is to make position three unambiguous before the phrase is ever spoken: under the anchor protocol, with wire one severed, my position three is the *second intact wire from the display end*, a definition Deaf can check with eyes alone (the second intact wire from the display end should be green). I also flag for Mute that the pattern 3 → 6 smells like a doubling sequence, so the manual's rule for the *next* stage — twelve, if Deaf's guess holds — should be extracted now, not after the cut. Alarm log for this round: hands report total silence and stillness. No cut — the phrase "confirmed, cut wire three now" has not been voiced.

